name: locate_colored_object_3d
summary: Locate a dominant-color object in calibrated RGB-D and estimate its visible three-dimensional geometry.

generality.rationale: The implementation is category-independent and useful across manipulation tasks, but is limited to separable HSV colors and one dominant component.
assumptions: The target has a supported dominant HSV color.
Registered metric depth and calibrated camera extrinsics are available.
The largest nearby same-color component represents one target object.
limitations: Same-color clutter can select or merge the wrong instance.
Transparent, reflective, heavily occluded, or background-colored objects are unreliable.
The returned axis and endpoints describe visible geometry, not a semantic object model.

level.rationale: It composes image segmentation, component selection, depth projection, frame transformation, and visible-geometry estimation into one observation.

composition.strategy: Currently monolithic; planned decomposition into segmentation, mask-to-point-cloud, and geometry-estimation atomic tools.

provenance.failure_gap: The baseline model lacked a configured detector and could not ground the color-described target in metric world coordinates.
evidence: stack-blocks-three iter_001: unchanged tool localized red, green, and blue blocks
